Hi Olga,

Thanks for the demo last week. Quick summary of our workload: 1) long-context retrieval/QA where typical inference uses ~100k tokens per session but 99th percentile of active context is closer to 60k, 2) a higher-concurrency embedding pipeline for search ranking (~200 qps), and 3) low-latency chat ops for support agents (P95 < 150ms).

We understand you offer Dedicated pools — we need recommendation on H100 vs A100 vs L4 for a two-year committed pool. Key asks: memory capacity for the long-context model, per-token latency for chat SLA, and a hedged SKU plan (reserved + burst) that keeps unit cost predictable. Can you also provide a short ops playbook for tiling/slotting and how fallthrough to burst works?

Attached: example query profile (we can send more telemetry if helpful).

Appreciate a quick runbook we can show procurement.

—Morgan

Quick technical readout from infra side:

Summary recommendations:
- Memory-first baseline: H100 (80GB) is the cleanest path for a single-host 100k-token KV cache for their long-context model. It preserves single-shot latency and avoids complex tiling.
- A100 40GB option: possible with split-tiling (shard attention heads and KV across slots) but introduces ~12-20% P95 penalty on generation due to cross-slot synchronization at large sequence lengths, and increases implementation complexity for our runtime (must orchestrate KV placement + offload to host memory).
- L4 (48GB) inference nodes: excellent for stateless workloads and short-context chat; they are cost-effective for burst and embedding QPS but are not suitable as the sole baseline for the 100k-token model.

Tiling/slotting notes:
- For A100 path, we recommend 2-way tiling for backbone and 4-way for KV depending on sequence distribution. This trades memory for latency and requires deterministic request routing to avoid cross-host locks.
- For H100 baseline, enable larger continuous KV cache with prefix caching and plan for pre-warm on expected active contexts.

Fallback and hedging:
- Recommended commit: 70% Reserved H100 capacity, 20% Reserved A100 (as a cheaper memory-sparse hedge), 10% L4 burst pool in a different fault domain for cost-effective scaling.
- Policy: route latency-sensitive chat to H100 or L4 depending on tokens-per-request; long-context generation to H100 primarily. If H100 capacity exhausted, failover to A100 with reduced max_context and explicit user-visible truncation warning via in-band metadata.

I'll attach a quick sim tomorrow with expected P95 regressions and tokens/dollar assumptions.

—Karthik
VP, Product Infrastructure

Attached is the pricing_matrix_v4.xlsx and tiling_sim_results_olga_v2.pdf — rough economics:
- Reserved H100 unit: $XX,XXX/month (tokens/dollar conservative). Memory-first workloads show 20-30% higher throughput per slot at long context relative to any tiled A100 configuration due to lower synchronization overhead.
- Reserved A100 unit: ~45-55% of H100 cost; when tiled you get headroom but need ~1.6x the A100 slots to approach H100 effective memory-per-sample for long contexts. That increases ops complexity and networking egress within cluster.
- L4 burst: cheapest tokens/dollar for stateless embeddings and short contexts — recommend as the burst/overflow pool.

Ops impact: hedged mix increases surface area for our SRE playbook (cross-pool routing, cache warming, model variant pinning). Estimate +1 engineer FTE for onboarding and runbook automation for the first 6 months.

Next steps: I recommend we propose the 70/20/10 reserved mix to Vectra with a clear early-exit fallback that reduces H100 reservation after the first quarter if telemetry shows lower active 100k-context sessions.

—Ben
